overview: The Rock Islands preserve traces of small Palauan communities whose descendants retain connections to ancestral places. Settlement change should be shown as movement and continuity, rather than the disappearance of a civilization.

items.text: Stone villages included terraces, house platforms and defensive walls. Earlier cave deposits preserve other forms of occupation.
Middens and other archaeological remains record the harvesting of marine resources in an environment of islands and lagoons.
Rock art and burials form part of the material record. Descendant traditions preserve places through stories, dances, proverbs and names.
In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries people left several stone villages for larger islands. This was relocation, not the extinction of Palauan culture.
Palauans continue to use these ancestral areas, with traditional resource governance remaining culturally important.

sources.title: UNESCO, Rock Islands Southern Lagoon
